name: Utah
one: Utah mails a ballot to every registered voter. Below: how to send it back and the deadlines.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Utah, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Getting your ballot

Friday, October 23Passed

A new ballot mailing address must reach your county clerk no later than 11 days before the election: Friday, October 23, 2026. The state's 2026 election page lists Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 5 p.m. as the last day to request a ballot. If you have not received your ballot shortly after October 27, contact your county clerk right away. You can check whether you are an active voter on the state's voter lookup. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be RECEIVED by your county clerk's office by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Ballots that arrive after November 3 are not counted, even if mailed earlier. A postmark is not enough. (official page)

That date has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Friday, October 30, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Utah’s own site

At school away from home, in Utah or in another state? What Utah says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Utah runs its elections mainly by mail: every active registered voter gets a ballot in the mail automatically. County clerks mail ballots for the November 3, 2026 election between October 13 and October 27. Inactive voters are not mailed a ballot unless they ask for one. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. You do not need to ask if you are an active voter. To have your ballot sent somewhere other than your home (for example to a college address), update your ballot mailing address online; you need a valid Utah driver license or Utah ID whose address matches your current address. Mail ballots are not forwarded. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Or fill out the paper alternate address form and send it to your county clerk's office. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Or update your ballot mailing address at your county clerk's office. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it early enough to arrive by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Some counties pay the postage and some do not (see your ballot's instructions); the state says the Postal Service will still deliver a ballot mailed without a stamp. (official page)
  • Drop box. Put it in a ballot drop box in your county before 8 p.m. on Election Day. Find drop boxes with the state's "How can I vote?" address search. (official page)
  • In person. Drop it off at an early voting location or at a polling place on Election Day. (official page)

What the envelope needs

No witness is needed. Before returning your ballot, sign the statement on the return envelope and write the last four digits of your Utah driver license or Utah ID card. Through 2028 you may give the last four digits of your Social Security number instead, and if you have none of these your ballot still counts if your signature matches the one on file. If your signature does not match, the county will notify you and you can send a form (a "cure letter") to confirm who you are. (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Utah’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 20, 2026 to Friday, October 30, 2026.

By state law, in-person early voting for a Tuesday election runs from 14 days before (Tuesday, October 20, 2026) through the Friday before (October 30, 2026). An election officer may extend it to the day before the election, so check your county's dates, hours and places. If you missed the registration deadline (5 p.m. Friday, October 23, 2026), you can still register in person at an early voting location or on Election Day with two forms of identification. (the law)

Students

At school in Utah, away from home

The state says a college student living away from home should register at the address they consider their permanent residence, which can be either the home address or the school address. To get your ballot at school while registered at home, update your ballot mailing address by October 23, 2026, since mail ballots are not forwarded. State law says your home does not change just because you are away as a student. (official page)

At school in another state, with Utah as home

The state's pages do not speak to students out of state separately. Its general rule (state law): you do not lose your Utah residence by moving to another state for a while if you mean to come back, and being a student away from Utah does not by itself change your residence; but you do lose it if you register or vote in the other state, or decide to make it your home. A Utah voter at school out of state can have their ballot sent there by updating their ballot mailing address by October 23, 2026. (the law)

Military and overseas

Active military members, their spouses and dependents, and voters living outside the U.S. can ask for a ballot online (with a Utah driver license or ID) or with a paper form sent to the county clerk, and can choose to get it by email, fax or mail (email or fax means giving up a secret ballot). By state law the request is on time if received before Election Day (by November 2, 2026). The ballot counts if your county clerk receives it by 8 p.m. Mountain Time on Election Day, or if you send it by 12:01 a.m. your local time on Election Day. The federal write-in ballot (FWAB) is a backup. (official page)

Utah in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • A mailed ballot must ARRIVE by 8 p.m. on Election Day; ballots received after November 3 are not counted, so a postmark does not help. Mail yours well ahead or use a drop box.
  • Beginning in 2029 Utah voters will get a ballot by mail only if they ask for one; state law requires a notice saying so in each ballot mailed through 2028.
  • The state's military and overseas page still gives last year's request date (Monday, November 3, 2025). State law says a military or overseas request is on time if it arrives before Election Day; for 2026 that means by Monday, November 2. Your county clerk can confirm.
  • Two request dates appear on the state's pages: a new ballot mailing address must reach the county clerk 11 days before the election (October 23), and the 2026 election page lists October 27 at 5 p.m. as the last day to request a ballot. We show both.

How this was checked

  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.
